# Codex 0.154.0 stream corpus

Replayed through `Parse` by `TestParseCorpus` in `internal/codex/corpus_test.go`.

`success.jsonl` is a real `codex exec --json` recording from a live review run, redacted by rewriting values only, using the `redactJSONValues` helper in `internal/codex/redact_test.go` (see `TestRedactJSONValuesPreservesEveryKey` there for the key-losslessness guarantee): `thread_id` and every finding's `evidence[].snapshot` were replaced with fixed placeholders, and the early preview `agent_message` text plus every `mcp_tool_call` result body were replaced with placeholder strings of the same JSON type. The final `agent_message` text was replaced with a synthetic result carrying the same shape (two findings, five reviewed files, no questions) as the original. `mcp_tool_call.arguments` was left untouched: its `snapshot` value is the fixed enum label `"workspace"`, not sensitive content, and its `path` values are already generic fixture-repo paths. No key present in the raw recording was deleted. This recording does not happen to exercise every shape this PR started tolerating (it predates codex-rs 0.154.0's `collab_tool_call`/`web_search` behavior and reports no `reasoning` items or `item.updated` events), which is what `tolerant-shapes.jsonl` below is for.

`split-findings.jsonl` and `missing-finding-title.jsonl` are constructed and pin the finding `title` contract: the first reports two findings on one action because the authorization check and the array-union `user_id` spoof need two independent fixes, the second omits `title` and must be refused.

`tolerant-shapes.jsonl`, `transient-error-then-success.jsonl` and `turn-failed.jsonl` are constructed, not recorded; they are the regression anchor for the shapes this PR added tolerance for. They follow the shapes verified against `codex-rs` at tag `rust-v0.154.0`: `tolerant-shapes.jsonl` exercises an unknown item type (`collab_tool_call`), a `web_search` item whose flattened object legally repeats the `id` key at the same level (the item's own id written first, the inner action's id second, `ThreadItemDetails`/`exec_events.rs` L97-102), a `reasoning` item, an `item.updated` event, an unrecognized turn usage key, and `cached_input_tokens` above `input_tokens`. `transient-error-then-success.jsonl` shows a `ModelRerouted`/`ConfigWarning`-class notification surfacing as a completed `error` item while the turn keeps running (`event_processor_with_jsonl_output.rs`, `CodexStatus::Running`). `turn-failed.jsonl` shows a `turn.failed` event carrying only the bare `error.message` the backend returned, because `protocol/src/error.rs`'s `extract_error_message` unwraps the provider's JSON envelope before the CLI ever writes it to the stream.
